source_title: India made ‘remarkable progress’ in reducing poverty: World Bank
source_excerpt: New Delhi India has over the last decade made “remarkable progress” in reducing poverty across both monetary and non-monetary dimensions, the World Bank said in a new report, adding the country saw one of the fastest reductions in poverty in the world. “Between 2011 and 2023, the share of the population living below the Lower Middle-Income Country line ($4.2/day) fell from 57.7% to 16.1%, lifting an estimated 496 million people out of poverty, while extreme poverty ($3.00/day) declined from 27.1% to 2.6%,” the World Bank said in its October 2026 Poverty and Equity Brief for India released on Friday (October 30, 2026). Shaping India’s multidimensional fight against poverty Shaping India’s multidimensional fight against poverty Inclusive development programmes such as the Samaveshi Aajeevika initiative of the Union government will help States identify vulnerability hotspots and target them Shaping India’s multidimensional fight against poverty storyline 1 Further, it said it projected poverty to continue declining, “albeit more gradually”, with the poverty rate as measured according to the $4.20/day line expected to fall from 14.2% in 2026 to 12.1% by 2028. “On the non-monetary dimensions, as measured by the Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative’s (OPHI) Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI), poverty fell sharply from 53.8% in 2005-06 to 16.4% in 2019-21, with the World Bank MPI measure at 15.5% in 2022-23,” the World Bank said. FM hails findings Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman welcomed the findings and, in a social media post, highlighted the various positive aspects the data revealed. Delhi registers decline in poverty, unemployment rate in recent years: DSIF report Delhi registers decline in poverty, unemployment rate in recent years: DSIF report Delhi State Indicator Framework 2025 report points out that the number of beneficiaries under the "Women in Distress" scheme in Delhi increased from 1,68,977 in 2015-16 to 3,97,465 in 2024-25 Delhi registers decline in poverty, unemployment rate in recent years: DSIF report storyline 1 “The World Bank identifies strong consumption growth, rising employment — especially among women — and expanded social transfers, including food subsidies, as major drivers,” Ms. Sitharaman said. “Under the leadership of Hon’ble PM Shri @narendramodi, the Government’s sustained policy efforts are yielding tangible results, strengthening the foundations for inclusive growth and greater economic opportunity,” she added. The World Bank’s October 2026 Poverty & Equity Brief records India’s progress as one of the fastest poverty declines in the world. The report highlights several significant gains: ✅ 49.6 crore people moved above the lower-middle-income poverty line of $4.20 a day between 2011 and 2023, with the poverty rate declining from 57.7% to 16.1%. ✅ Extreme poverty declined from 27.1% to 2.6% over the same period, measured at $3 a day. Both monetary poverty thresholds use 2021 purchasing power parity. ✅ Employment increased by 13.4 crore people between 2017 and 2023, nearly twice the increase in the working-age population. ✅ Rural women accounted for much of the employment gain, entering paid work and increasing the number of earners in their households. ✅ Both rural and urban households experienced substantial welfare gains, with faster progress in rural India narrowing the rural–urban gap. ✅ Access to electricity reached 99% of the population, according to the report’s 2022 survey data.
